input.question: Why do dogs have to sniff around a few minutes to find the perfect spot to take a crap?
input.ground_truth: Living things use senses to take in their surroundings. You see, smell, taste, feel, and hear. The sense that you use the most is probably your eyes. Dogs are different. They like to use their noses and smell just like we look around and see. They use sight and hearing too but they are not as important. So what dogs are doing is what they always do. The last time they were there the scents were different because of the wind. When you go outside and see the leaves are changing colors in the fall you look around. Dogs are similar. They just want to know whats changed.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do dogs have to sniff around a few minutes to find the perfect spot to take a crap?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine you are a dog. Before you go potty, you want to make sure the spot is just right. You want to know if other dogs have been there, if it’s safe, and if the ground is soft. So, you sniff and walk around to check everything out. That way, you pick the best, safest, and cleanest spot to do your business! Sniffing helps the dog feel safe and comfortable.
